question: How much compensation does EU law give for a cancelled flight of 1,500 km or less?
reference_answer: EUR 250 per passenger (Art. 7(1)(a)); it may be cut by 50% if re-routing arrives within 2 hours of the original arrival time, and it is not owed where the cancellation exceptions in Art. 5 apply.

question: My flight is delayed at departure by more than five hours and I no longer want to travel. Can I get my ticket refunded?
reference_answer: Yes. For a delay of at least five hours the airline must offer the assistance in Art. 8(1)(a): reimbursement of the ticket (and a return flight where relevant) (Art. 6(1)(iii)).

question: What care must the airline give me free of charge while I wait for a delayed or cancelled flight?
reference_answer: Meals and refreshments in reasonable relation to the waiting time, hotel accommodation when a stay of one or more nights (or an extra stay) becomes necessary, transport between airport and accommodation, and two telephone calls, emails, telexes or faxes (Art. 9).

question: I was downgraded from business to economy on a 2,000 km flight inside the EU. How much of the ticket price must be reimbursed?
reference_answer: 50% of the ticket price, within seven days (Art. 10(2)(b)); 30% applies to flights of 1,500 km or less and 75% to longer flights not under (a) or (b).

question: Within how many days must an airline pay my ticket refund after a cancellation?
reference_answer: Within seven days, by cash, bank transfer, bank order or cheque, or vouchers only with the passenger's signed agreement (Art. 8(1)(a) with Art. 7(3)).

question: Does the air passenger rights regulation protect me if I travel on a frequent flyer award ticket?
reference_answer: Yes. The regulation does not apply to free or reduced fares not available to the public, but it does apply to tickets issued under a frequent flyer or other commercial programme (Art. 3(3)).

question: At what moment does a flight count as having arrived when calculating the length of a delay?
reference_answer: When at least one of the aircraft doors is opened, on the assumption that passengers may then leave the aircraft (guidelines, section 3.3.3).

question: Is a strike by the airline's own staff an extraordinary circumstance that cancels my right to compensation?
reference_answer: No. According to the guidelines, the Court held that a strike by the operating carrier's staff linked to employment demands (e.g. pay) is not an extraordinary circumstance; this includes union and 'wildcat' strikes (section 5.2.2).

question: Does a bird strike count as an extraordinary circumstance for flight compensation?
reference_answer: Yes, a collision with a bird can be an extraordinary circumstance, and it is irrelevant whether it actually damaged the aircraft (guidelines, section 5.2.3).

question: Is there an EU-wide deadline for taking an airline to court over flight compensation?
reference_answer: No. Regulation 261/2004 sets no time limit; national limitation rules apply, so deadlines differ between Member States, and the Montreal Convention's 2-year limit is not relevant (section 9.2).

question: The airline moved my flight's departure more than one hour earlier. Is that treated as a cancellation?
reference_answer: Yes. The guidelines say a flight must be regarded as cancelled if the departure is brought forward by more than 1 hour, whereas postponing by less than 3 hours without other changes is not a cancellation (section 3.2.2).

question: My train arrived 75 minutes late. What compensation can I claim?
reference_answer: At least 25% of the ticket price for a delay of 60 to 119 minutes (50% for 120 minutes or more), unless the ticket was reimbursed under Art. 18 or an exemption applies (Art. 19(1)).

question: How quickly must a railway pay delay compensation, and can it pay me in vouchers?
reference_answer: Within one month of the request; vouchers or other services are allowed only if their terms are flexible, and the passenger can ask for money (Art. 19(7)).

question: My train has been cancelled. What choices must the railway undertaking offer me?
reference_answer: Where a delay of 60 minutes or more at the final destination is expected, or on cancellation: reimbursement (with a return service where relevant), continuation or re-routing at the earliest opportunity, or re-routing at a later date at the passenger's convenience (Art. 18(1)).

question: Am I allowed to take my bicycle on a train under the EU rail passenger rights regulation?
reference_answer: Yes, where appropriate for a reasonable fee, but railway undertakings may restrict it for safety or operational reasons such as peak-hour capacity, rolling stock or bicycle size (Art. 6(1),(3)).

question: Can a railway refuse delay compensation because its own staff were on strike?
reference_answer: No. Strikes by the railway undertaking's personnel are expressly not covered by the third-party exemption in Art. 19(10)(c).

question: Can I cancel my package holiday before it starts, and will I have to pay a fee?
reference_answer: Yes, at any time before the start, but the organiser may charge an appropriate and justifiable termination fee; no fee is due if unavoidable and extraordinary circumstances at or near the destination significantly affect the package or the travel there (Art. 12(1)-(2)).

question: What is the minimum limitation period for claiming compensation under the package travel directive?
reference_answer: Not less than two years (Art. 14(6)).

question: What help must the package organiser give me if I get into difficulty during the trip?
reference_answer: Appropriate assistance without undue delay, in particular information on health services, local authorities and consular assistance, and help with distance communications and alternative travel arrangements; a reasonable fee (not above actual costs) may be charged if the traveller caused the difficulty intentionally or negligently (Art. 16).

question: My 1,200 km flight was cancelled because a technical defect was found just before departure. Am I owed compensation, and how much?
reference_answer: Probably yes: according to the guidelines a technical problem inherent in the normal operation of the aircraft is not an extraordinary circumstance (section 5.2.2), so EUR 250 for a flight of 1,500 km or less (Art. 7(1)(a)), subject to the notice and re-routing conditions of Art. 5.

question: My flight arrived three and a half hours late. Can I get compensation even though the regulation only mentions compensation for cancellations?
reference_answer: Yes. Per the guidelines, the Court held that passengers arriving 3 hours or more late are entitled to the same Art. 7 compensation as for cancellation, unless extraordinary circumstances (section 4.4.7); the amount depends on distance (EUR 250/400/600, Art. 7).

question: If my flight is cancelled because of extraordinary circumstances, does the airline still have to provide meals and a hotel?
reference_answer: Yes. Extraordinary circumstances remove only the duty to pay compensation (Art. 5(3)); the duty of care still applies, even when such circumstances last a long time (guidelines, section 4.3.3).

question: My train was cancelled and nobody told me about re-routing options for two hours. Can I book a coach myself, and do I get meals while I wait?
reference_answer: Yes: if re-routing options are not communicated within 100 minutes of the scheduled departure, the passenger may contract other rail, coach or bus services and be reimbursed (Art. 18(3)); for a cancellation the railway must also offer meals and refreshments in reasonable relation to the waiting time (Art. 20(2)(a)).

question: A flight in my package holiday was cancelled. Can I claim compensation both from the package organiser and from the airline?
reference_answer: Yes, travellers may claim under both the directive and Regulation 261/2004, including directly from the airline even without a contract with it, but amounts granted under each are deducted from each other to avoid overcompensation (Art. 14(5); guidelines section 2.2.7).

question: The organiser of my package raised the price by 10% three weeks before departure. Is that allowed and what are my options?
reference_answer: An increase is allowed only if the contract reserves it, for fuel, taxes/fees or exchange rates, notified at least 20 days before the start (Art. 10(1),(3)); because it exceeds 8%, the traveller may accept it or terminate without a termination fee, with a refund within 14 days if no substitute is accepted (Art. 10(2), Art. 11(2),(5)).

question: My train arrives two hours late. If I take a refund of my ticket, can I also get delay compensation?
reference_answer: No: compensation is due for delays on tickets whose cost has not been reimbursed under Art. 18 (Art. 19(1)). Without a refund, a delay of 120 minutes or more gives at least 50% of the ticket price (Art. 19(1)(b)).
